docs.dcterms_abstract:
Her pleas to know the Parliament's desires concerning the settlement
of an allowance upon Her Highness the Princess Henrietta, who upon
the surrender of Exeter is under her care, not having been yet
answered she writes again to state her desire to remain about her
person without burdening Parliament or inconveniencing Lord and Lady
Northumberland; she points out that she deserves to be granted this
request. If it is not granted she asks to be reimbursed for the
money she has laid out while awaiting their Lordships' pleasure, and
for a pass for one to consult His Majesty without whose consent she
cannot deliver up his child; and meanwhile for a weekly allowance
for Her Highness and her family. "I have preserved Her Highness not
without many cares and fears from a weak to a very hopeful condition
of health".
